How does multi-profile support work with.answer:
When using the MCP Proxy for AWS with the AWS MCP Server, you can configure multiple AWS CLI profiles to switch between accounts or roles on a per-call basis. The proxy adds an `aws_profile` parameter to the server's auth-requiring tools, letting the agent route each request through a different set of credentials without restarting. 

To configure the proxy with multiple profiles, you can use the `--profile` flag or the `AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES` environment variable at startup. 

Example configuration:
```
AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES="prod-readonly dev staging"
```

Note that `AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES` takes precedence over `--profile` and `AWS_PROFILE` when set. 

Multi-profile switching requires SigV4 authentication with the MCP Proxy for AWS. OAuth authentication does not support this feature. If you use OAuth, each session is bound to a single IAM role and switching accounts requires re-authentication.

How can Amazon CloudSearch ignore unreco.answer: To ignore unrecognized document fields in Amazon CloudSearch, you can use dynamic fields. Specifically, you define a literal field called * and disable all indexing options for this field. This allows any unrecognized fields to inherit these options, meaning they will be added to your domain but will not be searchable or returnable, thus having minimal impact on the size of your index. This approach reduces upfront configuration and eliminates the need to modify your domain configuration when new attributes are added to products.

documents you are indexing. In some cases, however, you want to index a particular set of fields
and simply ignore everything else. You can use dynamic fields to ignore all unrecognized fields by
defining a literal field called * and disabling all indexing options for the field. Any unrecognized

fields will inherit those options and will be added to your domain; however, the field contents
won't be searchable or returnable, so they'll have minimal impact on the size of your index. (They
do, however, count toward the total number of fields configured for the domain.) Similarly, you can

Paginating Results in Amazon CloudSearch
By default, Amazon CloudSearch returns the top ten hits according to the specified sort order. To
control the number of hits returned in a result set, you use the size parameter.
To get the next set of hits beginning from a particular offset, you can use the start parameter.
